QF.id: VIII Sales Practices and Investor Protection Services_9

question.text: The code of conduct for stock brokers dealing in derivatives requires them to:

answer.text: Act with integrity, exercise due diligence, not indulge in manipulation, segregate client funds, and render fair and transparent service
Maximize their own profits at the expense of client interests
Share confidential client information with other brokers
Prioritize proprietary trading over client orders

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (Stock Brokers) Regulations, the code of conduct for stock brokers — including those dealing in derivatives — requires brokers to act with integrity, exercise due skill and diligence in execution, refrain from market manipulation or unfair trade practices, segregate client funds from their own, and render fair and transparent service to clients. Breach of the code can lead to penalties or suspension by SEBI/exchanges. The Trap: Profit maximisation at the expense of clients, sharing confidential client information, and prioritising proprietary trading over client orders are explicit violations of the code, not permitted conduct. Note: The bundled list of duties (integrity, due diligence, no manipulation, client-fund segregation, fair transparent service) is not laid out together in the cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook pages — those pages only refer in general terms to penalty/suspension grounds and to advice-related sales-agent conduct. The framing above reflects general SEBI broker code-of-conduct knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
